title.en: The future: going to, will, I'm coming

rule.en:
English has no single future tense. It has three common ways, each with its own job.

**going to** + the base form, for plans already made and for what you can see coming: **I'm going to visit Granny tomorrow.** **Look at those clouds! It's going to rain.**

**will** (short **'ll**, negative **won't**) + the base form, for what you decide as you speak, for offers and promises, and for what you think will happen: **I'll help you!** **I'll be quiet, I promise.** **It will be sunny tomorrow.**

The present continuous, for arrangements with a day or a time, often with other people: **I'm coming on Saturday.** **We're meeting Jack at ten.**

After **when** and **if**, use the present, not will: **When it stops raining, we'll play outside.**
rule.sl:
Angleščina nima enega samega prihodnjika, kot je slovenski *bom šel*. Ima tri pogoste načine, vsak za svoje.

**going to** + osnovna oblika, za načrte, ki jih že imamo, in za to, kar vidimo, da prihaja: **I'm going to visit Granny tomorrow.** (Jutri bom obiskal babico.) **Look at those clouds! It's going to rain.** (Poglej tiste oblake! Deževalo bo.)

**will** (kratko **'ll**, zanikano **won't**) + osnovna oblika, za to, kar se odločimo med govorjenjem, za ponudbe in obljube ter za to, kar mislimo, da bo: **I'll help you!** (Pomagal ti bom!) **I'll be quiet, I promise.** **It will be sunny tomorrow.**

*present continuous* za dogovore z dnevom ali uro, pogosto z drugimi ljudmi: **I'm coming on Saturday.** (V soboto pridem.) **We're meeting Jack at ten.**

Za **when** in **if** rabimo sedanjik, ne will, čeprav slovenščina reče bo: **When it stops raining, we'll play outside.** (Ko bo nehalo deževati, se bomo igrali zunaj.)
rule.it:
L'inglese non ha un solo futuro come l'italiano (andrò). Ha tre modi comuni, ognuno con il suo compito.

**going to** + forma base, per i progetti già decisi e per ciò che si vede arrivare: **I'm going to visit Granny tomorrow.** (Domani vado a trovare la nonna.) **Look at those clouds! It's going to rain.** (Guarda quelle nuvole! Sta per piovere.)

**will** (breve **'ll**, negativo **won't**) + forma base, per ciò che si decide mentre si parla, per offerte e promesse, e per ciò che si pensa succederà: **I'll help you!** (Ti aiuto io!) **I'll be quiet, I promise.** **It will be sunny tomorrow.**

Il *present continuous*, per gli appuntamenti fissati con un giorno o un'ora, spesso con altre persone: **I'm coming on Saturday.** (Vengo sabato.) **We're meeting Jack at ten.**

Dopo **when** e **if** si usa il presente, non will, anche dove l'italiano usa il futuro: **When it stops raining, we'll play outside.** (Quando smetterà di piovere, giocheremo fuori.)
rule.de:
Das Englische hat nicht ein Futur wie *werden*, sondern drei übliche Formen, jede mit ihrer Aufgabe. Das einfache Präsens wie in *Morgen fahre ich* reicht meist nicht.

**going to** + Grundform, für Pläne, die schon feststehen, und für das, was man kommen sieht: **I'm going to visit Granny tomorrow.** (Morgen besuche ich Oma.) **Look at those clouds! It's going to rain.** (Schau dir die Wolken an! Gleich regnet es.)

**will** (kurz **'ll**, verneint **won't**) + Grundform, für das, was man beim Sprechen beschließt, für Angebote und Versprechen und für Vermutungen: **I'll help you!** (Ich helfe dir!) **I'll be quiet, I promise.** **It will be sunny tomorrow.** Achtung: **I will** heißt nicht *ich will*, das ist **I want**.

Das *present continuous* für Verabredungen mit Tag oder Uhrzeit, oft mit anderen: **I'm coming on Saturday.** (Ich komme am Samstag.) **We're meeting Jack at ten.**

Nach **when** und **if** steht das Präsens, nicht will: **When it stops raining, we'll play outside.** (Wenn es aufhört zu regnen, spielen wir draußen.)

examples.en: Look at those clouds! It's going to rain.
examples.it: Guarda quelle nuvole! Sta per piovere.
examples.de: Schau dir die Wolken an! Gleich regnet es.

note.en: You can see it coming: going to.
note.de: Man sieht es kommen: going to.

examples.en: We're going to put the tent by the pond.
examples.it: Metteremo la tenda vicino allo stagno.
examples.de: Wir werden das Zelt am Teich aufstellen.

note.en: A plan already made: going to.
note.sl: Načrt, ki ga že imamo: going to.
note.it: Un progetto già deciso: going to.

examples.en: That bag looks heavy. I'll carry it!
examples.sl: Ta torba je videti težka. Daj, jaz jo nesem!
examples.it: Quella borsa sembra pesante. La porto io!
examples.de: Die Tasche sieht schwer aus. Ich trage sie!

note.en: Decided just now, an offer: will.
Arranged for a day: the present continuous.
note.it: Fissato per un giorno: present continuous.
note.de: Für einen Tag verabredet: present continuous.

examples.en: I think it will be sunny tomorrow.
examples.it: Penso che domani ci sarà il sole.
examples.de: Ich glaube, morgen wird es sonnig.

examples.en: When it stops raining, we'll play outside.
examples.sl: Ko bo nehalo deževati, se bomo igrali zunaj.
examples.it: Quando smetterà di piovere, giocheremo fuori.
examples.de: Wenn es aufhört zu regnen, spielen wir draußen.

note.en: After when: stops (the present), not will stop.
note.sl: Za when: stops (sedanjik), ne will stop.
note.it: Dopo when: stops (presente), non will stop.
note.de: Nach when: stops (Präsens), nicht will stop.
